# S1.1 A track is a black-box agent repo on this machine, and opening it shows that box's own site

## Requirement

> All vieb tracks now is though is just a side bar
>
> on my computer I basically like download the blackbox agent repos / And when you click each page that is eaxactly what it ends up showing.

Zach, Daily Note - Nov 24 2026, # Vibe tracks. Quoted exactly. [OBJECTIVES.md](../OBJECTIVES.md) lists every item; this note
explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

A track is one black-box agent repo (the blackbox_agent format: README, OBJECTIVES.md, specs/, feedback/,
ledger.jsonl, site/ …) in a folder on this machine. Clicking its row in the sidebar shows that box's own site in the
main pane, exactly as the box builds it (`site/index.html`, its dashboard under `site/dashboard/`), served locally.
Vibe Tracks draws nothing of its own inside a box's page. A box with no built site shows its README.

## Why

Each box already ships its full page (spec, feedback, iterations, gates, agents). Rebuilding those pages inside
Vibe Tracks is the work that made it "not that helpful" (W2 retro, Nov 21). The sidebar plus the box's own page is
the whole app, apart from the three roll-up pages (S3.1-S3.3).

## How it is checked

`S1.1 *` in the acceptance run: three fixture boxes, each with its own `site/index.html` carrying a marker text.
Clicking each row puts that box's marker on screen in the main pane (measured by its bounding box, not DOM presence),
and the address bar names the track. A fixture box with no `site/` shows its README's first heading.

# S1.2 A box holds nothing for Vibe Tracks, and tree changes never write a box

## Requirement

> I think a change is that the tracks are basically completley self contained and indpdent... / they really no nothign about each other.
>
> None of the agents should have a vibetracks.toml / each agent is compeltely indpdent and self contained.

Zach, Daily Note - Nov 24 2026, # Vibe tracks. Quoted exactly. [OBJECTIVES.md](../OBJECTIVES.md) lists every item; this note
explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

No box carries a Vibe Tracks file (no `vibetracks.toml`, no `vibe-parent:` key, nothing). No box names another
box. Moving, pinning, renaming, archiving or deleting a track in the sidebar changes Vibe Tracks' own file only: the
box's working tree and its git history are untouched. The only writes into a box are the box's own content a person
asked for, in the box's own format (a feedback note into its `feedback/`, S3.3).

## Why

Zach first suggested a `vibetracks.toml` per box, then reversed it the same evening. Boxes stay reusable on any
machine, with or without Vibe Tracks, and a box's git history stays about its work.

## How it is checked

`S1.2 *`: after a scripted run of every sidebar verb (drag, pin, rename, archive, move to section, delete) over the
fixture boxes, each box's `git status --porcelain` is empty, its HEAD is unchanged, and no file under any box
matches `*vibetrack*` or `*vibe-tracks*`. A fixture box with a `vibetracks.toml` dropped in by the test changes
nothing on the page (the file is ignored).

## Requirement

> Its vibe tracks that basically like defines that parent child relationship.

Zach, Daily Note - Nov 24 2026, # Vibe tracks. Quoted exactly. [OBJECTIVES.md](../OBJECTIVES.md) lists every item; this note
explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

Which track sits under which, in what order, what is pinned, which named sections exist and what is
archived are all kept in Vibe Tracks' own file(s), outside every box. A person can read and edit that file by hand
(Principle #1, parity), and a hand edit shows in the sidebar within a tick. The same box can be listed once.

## Why

The parent/child relationship is a fact about how Zach organises his work, not about any box. Keeping it in one
place is what lets boxes stay independent (S1.2) and lets a drag reorganise everything (S2.8).

## How it is checked

`S1.3 *`: the tree set by drags survives a `vt serve` restart; the file that changed lives outside every box;
editing that file by hand (moving one entry under another) moves the row in the sidebar within 5 s with no reload.

# S2.8 Drag to reorder and to move under another track, on a stock tree component

## Requirement

> and it supports that easily we can just like drag to reorder the tracks in the side bar.
>
> (So I think we should deinftily use like a stock tree here etc to get thoose nice folder/drag and drop reordering interactions)

Zach, Daily Note - Nov 24 2026, # Vibe tracks. Quoted exactly. [OBJECTIVES.md](../OBJECTIVES.md) lists every item; this note
explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

In the Parent grouping, dragging a row between two rows reorders it; dropping it onto a row makes it that
row's child; dragging it out to the left makes it top-level. A drop line or a highlighted target shows where it will
land before the drop. A track can never be dropped into its own subtree. The same moves work from the keyboard. The
tree model and drag behaviour come from a stock component, not hand-rolled code; the rows keep Claude's look (S2.2).

## Why

Zach's ask, and [[feedback_availability_before_originality]]. The prior-art sweep (Nov 24) picks Headless Tree's
`@headless-tree/core` (MIT, no dependencies, ordered drag with reparenting, keyboard; renders nothing, so the Claude
rows stay) with Atlassian Pragmatic drag and drop as the fallback; react-arborist and @atlaskit/tree need React and
Wunderbaum draws its own rows.

## How it is checked

`S2.8 *`: real pointer drags (Playwright mouse down/move/up) for each of the four moves, the drop indicator's box
measured mid-drag, the result read back after a restart; a drop into its own child is refused; the keyboard path does
one reorder. Which library is used is checked by the page loading a known stock tree package, named in
`ruler/reference/stock-trees.json`.

# S4.3 Local-only by default; publishing to GitHub is an option that needs `gh` signed in

## Requirement

> vibetracks should require that you are loged into github btw. beacuse then it will kinda like make a new github repo for you...
>
> wella ctually that should be an option wether you want to publish it yet or not we should support local only tracks.

Zach, Daily Note - Nov 24 2026, # Vibe tracks. Quoted exactly. [OBJECTIVES.md](../OBJECTIVES.md) lists every item; this note
explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

Without `--publish`, nothing leaves the machine and no GitHub sign-in is needed. With `--publish`, `vt new`
checks `gh auth status` before making anything; signed out, it stops, names `gh auth login`, and creates nothing.
Signed in, it creates a **private** repo (public only with `--public`) and pushes the first commit. A local track can be
published later from its ··· menu (Open in › shows GitHub once it is).

## Why

His correction in the same breath: GitHub is an option, local-only tracks are supported. Private by default:
a first public push is a step nothing undoes.

## How it is checked

`S4.3 *`: with a fake `gh` on PATH that records its arguments: no `--publish` → never called; signed out → exit
non-zero, message names `gh auth login`, no folder made; signed in → `repo create <name> --private --source <dir>
--push` called once.
